subject: after the naming
fact: The official trial and judgment of Alkrist will occur after the naming ceremony, when the new head of the Avowed assumes power — delaying accountability and ensuring Bookwyrm’s influence endures.
source_quote: That will be done after the naming, by the new head of the Avowed.

subject: elapsed time
fact: An hour passes between two events in the session.
source_quote: An hour later

subject: evening in Deneir's Sanctum
fact: The events in Deneir's Sanctum occur during the evening hours, following the opening of the safe; the group waits until later this evening before being escorted to their chambers.

subject: naming ceremony
fact: The formal naming ceremony for the next head of the Candlekeep Avowed is scheduled for tomorrow, marking the critical turning point in the political maneuvering around Bookwyrm’s fate.
source_quote: Tomorrow morning's naming ceremony clearly will not name her.

subject: session date
fact: The events described occur during the ongoing session following the restoration of Daral and preceding the ambush — a single narrative unit with no external calendar reference.
source_quote: Combat?" Zalthir said. Yes. Combat.

subject: session date
fact: The events described occurred during a single session of roleplay, culminating in the strategic planning phase and the tense confrontation with Bookwyrm — no calendar date is given, but temporal continuity is maintained.
source_quote: I wrote it down either way.

subject: Session Date
fact: The events occurred during the continuation of a campaign session following the healing of Daral and the discovery of the helmed horrors’ ambush.
source_quote: [Continuing — Speaker: Grygum, Scene: Waiting in Deneir's Sanctum]

subject: Session date
fact: The events occurred during the ongoing session, following the ambush of the helmed horrors and preceding any further investigation into the key’s origin.
source_quote: Quiet, then. Glass on the floor, dust settling...

subject: Session Date
fact: The events occurred on the day of the naming ceremony, immediately preceding the formal transition of leadership in the Avowed.
source_quote: That will be done after the naming, by the new head of the Avowed.

subject: session date
fact: The session occurs on the 5th day of the 2nd Tenday of Taraskh 1493 DR.
source_quote: On the 5th day of the 2nd Tenday of Taraskh 1493

subject: session date
fact: The session occurs on the day of the ambush in Deneir's Sanctum.
source_quote: ## Thorin — Ambush of the Helmed Horrors

subject: tomorrow
fact: The naming ceremony for the new head of the Avowed is scheduled for tomorrow, marking the next critical turning point in the political maneuvering surrounding Bookwyrm.
source_quote: Tomorrow there will be a naming ceremony.

subject: Academic principle vs justice
fact: The group debated whether academic rigor (requiring three evidentiary types) outweighs practical justice (concluding guilt from confession and context).
source_quote: What matters more to an academic? Putting the murderer in jail, or being true to their academic principles and their research proposal?

subject: accusation of accomplices
fact: The group publicly acknowledged the existence of accomplices without naming Bookwyrm.
source_quote: Yeah — we know there are accomplices

subject: A'lai's political position
fact: A'lai will not be named the new head of Candlekeep — suspicion extends to him as well.
source_quote: A'lai won't be named either.

subject: Alkrist's confession
fact: Alkrist confessed to killing Janussi under Kalan's spell, and the confession was deemed insufficient by academic standards despite being legally valid.
source_quote: Alkrist had confessed. Kalan Strongbranch hadn't yet come back into the room, and we knew there was a thread running from all this back to A'lai.

subject: Alkrist's confession
fact: Alkrist publicly confessed to murdering Janussi under magical compulsion, ending the investigation and shifting responsibility to Kalan Strongbranch.
source_quote: Alkrist had said it out loud, in the room, with Kalan's spell still holding him honest — he'd killed Janussi.

subject: Alkrist's confession
fact: Alkrist's confession under the Zone of Truth spell provided the first concrete breakthrough in the case, but lacked corroborating evidence to identify the mastermind behind the murder.
source_quote: Alkrist had said it out loud, in the room, with Kalan's spell still holding him honest — he'd killed Janussi.

subject: ambush of the helmed horrors
fact: An unexpected ambush occurred in Deneir's Sanctum, where three helmed horrors attacked the party, targeting Daz repeatedly, forcing the group to adapt tactics after realizing the creatures lack minds and respond only to force.
source_quote: Glass and wood came in at the same time, from three directions, and for a breath none of us had moved.

subject: Ambush of the Helmed Horrors
fact: Three helmed horrors breached Deneir's Sanctum through windows, targeting Daz and later Grygum upon key transfer, ultimately destroyed by coordinated party efforts after revealing their mechanical, non-sentient nature.
source_quote: Glass and wood came in at the same time, from three directions, and for a breath none of us had moved.

subject: Ambush of the Helmed Horrors
fact: Three helmed horrors breached the chamber through the windows, targeting the key in Daz’s pocket, and were systematically destroyed after shifting focus when the key changed hands.
source_quote: Three suits of murderous plate had come through the windows to die for it.

subject: Bookwyrm's potential dismissal
fact: Bookwyrm may be dismissed from her position due to suspicion, with the new head of Candlekeep likely to demand a Zone of Truth as her first act.
source_quote: The new head may give Bookwyrm one of two choices: continue as a member of the Avowed, or submit to a Zone of Truth.

subject: Bookwyrm's relief
fact: Bookwyrm was relieved, not heartbroken, upon learning of Alkrist's confession.
source_quote: Alkrist. I could never have imagined it.

subject: Candlekeep naming ceremony
fact: A formal naming ceremony for the next head of the Avowed is scheduled for tomorrow, and Kalan believes the suspicion surrounding Bookwyrm will ensure she is not chosen — making her vulnerable to post-ceremony scrutiny and potential removal.
source_quote: Tomorrow morning's naming ceremony clearly will not name her.

subject: combat outcome
fact: The helmed horrors were destroyed through coordinated attacks using fire, acid, brute force, and tactical positioning, leaving only rusted wreckage.
source_quote: The suit came apart where it stood, and the last of them folded down into piles of rust and loose plate, like they'd never been anything but junk somebody stacked up.

subject: Dawnbringer’s Lesser Restoration
fact: Dawnbringer performed a lesser restoration on Daral, curing his illness and triggering his epiphany about magical swords — an event that awakened the sword’s sentience and began a new dynamic between scholar and weapon.
source_quote: The blade lit, poured into Daral, and took the sickness with it.

subject: Dawnbringer's psychic communication
fact: Dawnbringer communicated telepathically with the narrator, expressing a need for further therapy sessions after a productive first session, and the narrator acknowledged her as 'she' despite uncertainty.
source_quote: *I'm not leaving here without the therapy. That first session was actually very productive.*

subject: Dawnbringer's Restoration of Daral
fact: Dawnbringer is used to restore Daral from sickness, causing him to straighten, breathe, and become ecstatic, which triggers his sudden scholarly obsession with the sword's sentience and beauty.
source_quote: The blade lit, poured into Daral, and took the sickness with it. He straightened. He breathed. In the space of a heartbeat he was a well man, and he was ecstatic. ... 'I shall do all kinds of new research on magical swords,' he announced, 'with the sentience and the beauty of Dawnbringer. I intend to make it an area of active research.'

subject: Dawnbringer's telepathic communication
fact: Dawnbringer communicates telepathically — her voice clicks inside the speaker’s skull like a palm slapping stone.
source_quote: And then a click inside my skull, a sound like a palm slapping stone, whatever that was supposed to mean.

subject: Dawnbringer's telepathy
fact: Dawnbringer demonstrated the ability to communicate telepathically with the narrator, producing a distinct mental sound like a palm slapping stone, confirming her non-human nature.
source_quote: a click inside my skull, a sound like a palm slapping stone, whatever that was supposed to mean.

subject: Dawnbringer's therapy request
fact: Dawnbringer requested therapy — she said, 'I'm not leaving here without the therapy. That first session was actually very productive.'
source_quote: She spoke up in my head. *I'm not leaving here without the therapy. That first session was actually very productive. I really feel we need to—*

subject: Daz
fact: Daz noticed the woman was delighted to have them wrapped up and out of everything.
source_quote: Daz found the other half, the half I only saw land on his face: she was delighted to have us wrapped up and out of everything, no more heads poking anywhere.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz noticed the woman was not sad but relieved.
source_quote: Daz caught it too — I saw him go quiet and still, the way he does when he's found the seam in a thing. She was not sad. She was relieved.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz refused to touch the cup of tea.
source_quote: Daz did not touch the cup in front of him.

subject: Daz's contingency plan
fact: Daz's contingency plan is to 'start hacking and slashing' if things go sideways — a comfort, not a strategy.
source_quote: If things go sideways, we can always start hacking and slashing.

subject: Daz's floor strategy
fact: Daz provides a floor — hacking and slashing — as a fallback when all strategy fails.
source_quote: If things go sideways, we can always start hacking and slashing.

subject: Fembris Lancer's expected election
fact: Fembris Lancer is expected to be elected the new Avowed, replacing Bookwyrm due to suspicion.
source_quote: Fembris Lancer will probably get elected the new avowed.

subject: Fembris's punishment
fact: Fembris Lancer was assigned to keep the adventurers company as his penance.
source_quote: Fembris Lancer was already in there, serving out his own punishment by keeping us company.

subject: food taster protocol
fact: The group established an informal food taster protocol using Fembris Lancer, with Daz's '118' signaling his selection; he ate without harm, reinforcing the group's survivalist pragmatism.

subject: Glabbagool's satisfaction
fact: Glabbagool was pleased with the stolen potion of flying and deemed it a good skill.
source_quote: I like the flying skill. That was a good skill.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum handed the key back to Daz after it had been passed to him.
source_quote: When Grygum handed the key to Daz — who saw it?

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum kept his feet steady as the last helmed horror reached for him, refusing to be moved.
source_quote: Grygum kept his feet like the floor was the one thing he wasn't giving up.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum lifted the cup and let the tea run down into Glabbagool instead of down his throat.
source_quote: I lifted the cup, tilted it to my mouth, and let the tea run down into Glabbagool instead of down my throat.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum marked in the margin that they had come all this way to convict a woman not of murder but of embarrassment.
source_quote: I only took notes and marked, in the margin, that we had come all this way to convict a woman not of murder but of embarrassment

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum noticed Daral had stopped bragging and was complimenting the party up and down.
source_quote: He'd stopped bragging. That was new. He was complimenting the party up and down, which for Daral was a kind of surrender.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum noticed Fembris Lancer had no reservations about the food.
source_quote: Fembris, on the other hand, had no such reservations — come, come, come, already reaching, all appetite and no suspicion.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum noticed that the helmed horrors went for Daz first, then for him when the key changed hands.
source_quote: The suits had gone straight for Daz, then straight for Grygum the second the key changed hands.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum noticed the room stopped looking at the safe and started looking at each other after finding the red herring coin.
source_quote: The whole room understood that at once, and at once stopped looking at the safe and started looking at each other.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum noticed the woman said 'beloved by all'.
source_quote: Did she actually say 'beloved by all'? Of course she did. Beloved by all.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum noticed the woman was sincerely afraid something would happen to them.
source_quote: I looked at her while she said it and found, underneath, that she meant the worry. It was real — she was sincerely afraid something would happen to us.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum realized the woman did not have the sapphire when the spell found nothing.
source_quote: I reached out with the spell and found nothing where the sapphire should have been. Bookwyrm did not have it.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum stepped up and unleashed a burst of clean light that caught two helmed horrors at once.
source_quote: Grygum stepped up and let go a burst of clean light that caught two of them at once, both flinching under it.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum understood that Daz's number '118' meant Fembris had been promoted as taster.
source_quote: Daz offered, which meant nothing to Fembris and everything to us

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum's Glabbagool arm swiped the potion of flying off the table.
source_quote: While she was talking, I had my Glabbagool arm swipe the potion of flying off the table.

subject: House arrest avoidance
fact: The adventurers were not under house arrest, but were escorted to Deneir's Sanctum for protection.
source_quote: No, no, no. You currently hold the most important evidence... I'm simply doing this to protect you.

subject: Infamous definition clarification
fact: The term 'infamous' was questioned and confirmed to mean 'extra famous' — a bad joke that earned a half-groan.
source_quote: Infamous," I said. "You know that's supposed to mean extra famous.

subject: Janussi’s murder investigation
fact: The investigation into Janussi’s murder has reached a turning point: Alkrist has confessed under magical compulsion, the heart was moved to a statue’s chalice, and Bookwyrm is the prime suspect for concealment — but no physical evidence directly ties her to the crime, forcing the group to rely on strategy over proof.
source_quote: You have a confession, a heart, and a cleaver.

subject: Kalan reinstated
fact: Kalan Strongbranch was reinstated as head of the Avowed after the investigation.
source_quote: Would you be so willing as to take your position once more?

subject: Kalan's firing
fact: Kalan Strongbranch was dismissed from his position prior to solving Janussi’s murder, making the resolution of the case both a redemption and an ironic twist.
source_quote: Kalan had gotten fired. That's the terrain — a man told he was done, standing next to a case he couldn't crack, that we cracked for him.

subject: Kalan's moral compromise
fact: Kalan plans to give Bookwyrm a chance to decline the Zone of Truth — knowing refusal implies guilt, making her politically untenable.
source_quote: We will give her the opportunity to decline. Her declining will further weaken her support among the other Avowed.

subject: Kalan's offer to give full report to Bookwyrm
fact: Kalan offered to give Bookwyrm a full report of the evidence against her, to pressure her into declining the position — thus implying guilt without direct accusation.
source_quote: I will give it to Bookwyrm herself.

subject: Kalan's patient strategy
fact: Kalan advocates patience — letting suspicion and the naming ceremony do the work instead of direct confrontation.
source_quote: Sometimes the clever play is to be patient.

subject: Kalan's refusal to sneak
fact: Kalan refused to cast the Zone of Truth spell covertly again, insisting on a public, bold demand for submission — a shift motivated by fear of future consequences rather than principle.
source_quote: I will not sneak this time. We will walk in, and we will boldly demand that she submit to a Zone of Truth.

subject: Kalan's shift from stealth to open confrontation
fact: Kalan changed from covert casting of Zone of Truth to demanding open submission — motivated by fear of future repercussions.
source_quote: I will not sneak this time. We will walk in, and we will boldly demand that she submit to a Zone of Truth.

subject: Kalan's shift to patient strategy
fact: Kalan abandoned direct confrontation and instead planned to wait for Bookwyrm’s political isolation, then use the reward to obtain a magical book that would prove her culpability after the fact.
source_quote: If you do it after the fact, that's much better.

subject: Kalan Strongbranch's firing
fact: Kalan Strongbranch was fired — a man told he was done, standing next to a case he couldn't crack, that we cracked for him.
source_quote: Kalan had gotten fired. That's the terrain — a man told he was done, standing next to a case he couldn't crack, that we cracked for him.

subject: lesser restoration usage
fact: A lesser restoration was cast on Daral, removing his sickness and restoring him to health, which he then used to begin research.
source_quote: a lesser restoration I now got to keep in the bank. The blade lit, poured into Daral, and took the sickness with it. He straightened. He breathed. In the space of a heartbeat he was a well man...

subject: naming ceremony
fact: The naming ceremony for the new head of the Avowed will occur tomorrow and is expected to exclude Bookwyrm and A'lai, with Fembris Lancer likely to be elected, creating an opportunity to pressure Bookwyrm into submitting to a Zone of Truth.
source_quote: Tomorrow there will be a naming ceremony.

subject: naming ceremony
fact: The naming ceremony will determine the next head of the Avowed at Candlekeep, and is expected to exclude Bookwyrm and A'lai due to suspicion, paving the way for Fembris Lancer.
source_quote: Tomorrow morning's naming ceremony clearly will not name her.

subject: offering Bookwyrm a chance to decline
fact: Kalan plans to offer Bookwyrm the opportunity to decline the headship before the naming ceremony, ensuring that any refusal will be interpreted as guilt and further erode her support among the Avowed.
source_quote: We will give her the opportunity to decline.

subject: one more thing
fact: One more thing happens after she believes she has won.
source_quote: one more thing

subject: Opening of Alkrist's Safe
fact: The safe containing Alkrist’s possessions was opened and revealed a potion of flying, a healing potion, a heap of gold coins, and one red coin stamped with a herring — the only tangible clue, which was later identified as a red herring.
source_quote: Inside: a potion of flying, a healing potion, a heap of gold coins, and nothing at all that pointed anywhere. Thorin asked whether there was a red herring in there. There was, in fact — one of the coins had a herring stamped on it, and it was red.

subject: safe opening
fact: The opening of Alkrist’s safe reveals a potion of flying, healing potion, gold, and a red herring coin — but no direct evidence of guilt, causing the Avowed to shift blame and abandon investigation, allowing Bookwyrm to control the narrative.
source_quote: Nothing else in there implicated Alkrist of anything.

subject: safe sealed
fact: The safe was sealed with its contents declared of no interest.
source_quote: They closed the safe with everything still inside... and declared it of no interest.

subject: taster selection
fact: Fembris Lancer was chosen as the taster for the food with the number 118.
source_quote: I'd say 118

subject: tea refusal
fact: Daz and Thorin publicly refused Bookwyrm’s tea as a gesture of distrust, making themselves visibly antagonistic — an overt move that Grygum avoided by covertly diverting the tea into Glabbagool.
source_quote: Daz did not touch the cup in front of him. 'I'm certainly not drinking any tea from somebody we suspect may have done this.'

subject: The Accusation of Alkrist
fact: Alkrist was publicly accused of a grave crime by the Leader, based on unverified testimony from an unnamed source; the accusation was used to redirect suspicion away from the true conspirators.
source_quote: She had named her the mastermind. Thin.

subject: the appointment of Kalan Strongbranch
fact: Bookwyrm reinstated Kalan Strongbranch as head of the Avowed, acknowledging his methodology had proven its merit, despite his prior removal.
source_quote: Well, it would seem, Kalan, that your methodology has proven its merit. Well done. ... Would you be so willing as to take your position once more?

subject: the click in the narrator's skull
fact: A psychic click, likened to a palm slapping stone, occurred in the narrator’s mind during Dawnbringer’s telepathic communication, signaling an unexplained but impactful moment of connection.
source_quote: a click inside my skull, a sound like a palm slapping stone

subject: the closing of Alkrist's safe
fact: The safe was closed with all contents inside — including the potion of flying — and declared of no interest, despite the potion having been stolen moments before.
source_quote: They closed the safe with everything still inside — the gold, the herring, the healing — and declared it of no interest.

subject: the discovery of Bookwyrm's fear and delight
fact: Grygum observed that Bookwyrm was both sincerely afraid something would happen to the adventurers and delighted to have them isolated and out of the way.
source_quote: I looked at her while she said it and found, underneath, that she meant the worry. It was real — she was sincerely afraid something would happen to us. Daz found the other half, the half I only saw land on his face: she was delighted to have us wrapped up and out of everything, no more heads poking anywhere.

subject: The Discovery of the Key's Purpose
fact: After the battle, the party deduces that the helmed horrors were not targeting individuals but were drawn exclusively to the inert key, which emitted no magical signature but was the sole object of their aggression.
source_quote: They weren't following a face. They were following the key itself, sniffing it out through plate and pocket both. ... The reason you picked helmed horrors as assassins is they can't talk. Literally.

subject: the escort to Deneir's Sanctum
fact: The adventurers were escorted to Deneir's Sanctum under the pretense of protection, but in reality to isolate them from further investigation.
source_quote: I'm simply doing this to protect you. As you so correctly pointed out, there are other criminal elements within the society, and I would hate for something terrible to happen to you.

subject: the final declaration of no trial
fact: Bookwyrm declared that today was not a day for trials and juries, and that the matter would be resolved after the naming by the new head of the Avowed.
source_quote: But today is not a day for trials and juries. That will be done after the naming, by the new head of the Avowed.

subject: the final escort to chambers
fact: After being held in Deneir's Sanctum, the adventurers were to be escorted to their chambers later that evening, under Kalan's supervision.
source_quote: I will now ask Kalan Strongbranch to escort you to Deneir's Sanctum. ... where you will wait until later this evening, then be escorted to your chambers.

subject: the food tasting protocol
fact: The group established a taster protocol using Fembris Lancer, assigning him the role of '118' to consume food before the others, and he survived without incident.
source_quote: I'd say 118," ... "Fembris ate on, blessedly unaware that he had just been promoted.

subject: theft of the potion of flying
fact: The potion of flying was stolen from Alkrist's safe by Glabbagool's arm while the room was distracted, and no one noticed the theft.
source_quote: Glabbagool's arm came out low and quiet... It closed around the vial, drew it back, and no one turned. Not one head.

subject: theft of the potion of flying
fact: The potion of flying was stolen from the Alkrist safe by Glabbagool's arm while the Avowed were distracted by the red herring coin; no one noticed, and the safe was resealed with everything else inside.

subject: the group's decision to call Alkrist's accomplices
fact: The group chose to say only that there were accomplices in Janussi's death, avoiding direct accusation of Bookwyrm to maintain plausible deniability.
source_quote: Yeah — we know there are accomplices," I said.

subject: The group's final agreement
fact: The group agrees to hand the case to Kalan, wait for the naming ceremony, and use their reward to obtain a book that proves Bookwyrm's guilt.
source_quote: Alright, so we've got to nail Bookwyrm... We use our reward to access the thing that will do her in.

subject: The Helmed Horrors' Ambush
fact: Three helmed horrors enter Deneir's Sanctum through broken glass and wood, target Daz for the key in his pocket, attack Grygum after the key is transferred, and are ultimately destroyed one by one through fire, acid, and physical strikes.
source_quote: Glass and wood came in at the same time, from three directions, and for a breath none of us had moved. ... The first one went straight for Daz. ... The third one shoved past Grygum like he wasn't there and reached for Daz's throat. ... The horror on Daz landed one square. ... The horror on Grygum reached, missing, reaching, missing — Grygum kept his feet like the floor was the one thing he wasn't giving up. ... The suit came apart where it stood, and the last of them folded down into piles of rust and loose plate.

subject: The Locked Door in Deneir's Sanctum
fact: After Daral is healed and the battle ends, the party discovers the door to Deneir's Sanctum remains locked, trapping them despite their victory and leaving them to wonder how the story will end.
source_quote: Then Daral, glowing and cured and full of research, rose to leave — and found the door still locked. He was not going anywhere. None of us were. So we sat in Deneir's office, fed by proxy, our patient healed, wondering how the story was going to end.

subject: the request to cure Daral
fact: Daral asked the group whether they would cure him of his condition, revealing his fear of being left broken and unworthy of the spell.
source_quote: Are you guys going to cure me or anything?" ... "under the scholarship, the small fear of being left broken because we'd decided he wasn't worth the spell.

subject: the revelation of Bookwyrm's relief
fact: Bookwyrm's tears and heartbreak over Alkrist's betrayal were observed by Grygum and Daz to be performative, masking genuine relief that the blame had shifted.
source_quote: The tears were correct and the eyes behind them were doing something else. Daz caught it too — I saw him go quiet and still, the way he does when he's found the seam in a thing. She was not sad. She was relieved.

subject: The three evidentiary types
fact: The group identifies three elements: confession, heart, cleaver — and debates whether they constitute three types of evidence.
source_quote: You have a confession. A heart and a cleaver.

subject: the use of the Locate Object spell
fact: Grygum cast Locate Object to detect a sapphire on Bookwyrm, but found nothing, confirming she did not possess it.
source_quote: I reached out with the spell and found nothing where the sapphire should have been. Bookwyrm did not have it.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin notices Dawnbringer making noises in his head and interprets it as communication.
source_quote: She could make noises in my head, so — yeah. That was answer enough for the mechanics of it.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin realizes the word 'infamous' means 'extra famous' and says it aloud.
source_quote: Infamous," I said. "You know that's supposed to mean extra famous.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin refused to drink the tea.
source_quote: Yeah, I'm not drinking the tea, that's for sure,

subject: Thorin's final solution
fact: Thorin's final solution is to use the reward to obtain a magic book that proves Bookwyrm’s guilt after the fact — avoiding suspicion during the process.
source_quote: We use our reward to access the thing that will do her in. That's much better.

subject: Thorin's Proposal to Use a Dead Horror as a Divining Rod
fact: After the battle, Thorin proposes repurposing a destroyed helmed horror as a magical divining tool to detect who else possesses the inert key, suggesting a novel application of the enemy's remains.
source_quote: Can we grab one of them and use it to detect who else has the key?" I said. "Turn it into a sort of divining rod, as it were.

subject: Thorin's pursuit of physical evidence
fact: Thorin sought physical evidence tying Bookwyrm to placing the heart in the chalice, but was reminded that concealment is not commission.
source_quote: Is there any physical evidence, anything else, we can bring to bear here?

subject: Thorin's realization of academic irony
fact: Thorin realizes that Kalan’s own academic standard now protects the person they want to convict — the irony is noted.
source_quote: I filed that quietly under the column marked *irony*. The man wrote the standard, and the standard he wrote now shelters the person we most want to reach.

subject: travel to key location
fact: The key in Daz's pocket is the target of the helmed horrors, drawn to it through plate and pocket alike, with no regard for person or spell.
source_quote: Daz passed the key to Grygum and threw the last of what he had at the one he'd been burning — three darts of light, all home. And the horror turned on a coin and went for Grygum instead... They weren't following a face. They were following the key itself, sniffing it out through plate and pocket both.

subject: travel to Sloobludop
fact: Sloobludop is approximately eight days away via the Darklake.
source_quote: the town of Sloopdopblop is just eight days away

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir notices that Kalan did not discount the confession when listing evidence.
source_quote: He said: you have a confession. A heart and a cleaver. Right — but he didn't discount the confession.

subject: Zalthir's question about the confession's wording
fact: Zalthir questioned whether Kalan’s phrasing — 'you have a confession, a heart, and a cleaver' — implied that the confession was not discounted, despite its insufficiency under academic standards.
source_quote: He said: you have a confession. A heart and a cleaver.

subject: Zalthir's sentence-worrying
fact: Zalthir obsesses over wording — repeatedly questioning how phrases were spoken to extract meaning.
source_quote: Zalthir went back to the wording, which is his instinct — worry the sentence until it gives.

subject: Zone of Truth spell mechanics
fact: The Zone of Truth spell does not guarantee truth — it reveals whether the target can lie, making resistance detectable.
source_quote: The spell doesn't hand you the truth. It hands you the ability to watch someone refuse it.

subject: Avowed
fact: The Avowed are the governing body of Candlekeep, whose members will vote on Bookwyrm’s fate during the naming ceremony, influenced by suspicion and academic protocol rather than direct evidence.
source_quote: The new head may give Bookwyrm one of two choices: continue as a member of the Avowed, or submit to a Zone of Truth.

subject: Builders of the Helmed Horrors
fact: The builders deliberately designed the helmed horrors to be mute and mindless, ensuring no interrogation was possible — they were chosen precisely to eliminate witnesses and resist manipulation.
source_quote: A killer with no mouth and no mind — whoever built these chose them precisely so there'd be nobody to squeeze afterward.

subject: Candlekeep
fact: Candlekeep operates as a hierarchical institution where authority transitions matter — the new head of Candlekeep will be eager to provide incriminating magical texts to those who have earned reward and goodwill, making institutional power a weapon.
source_quote: the book will come from the new head of Candlekeep — who will be delighted to give it to you.

subject: Candlekeep Avowed
fact: The Avowed are the governing body of Candlekeep, currently divided by suspicion around Bookwyrm’s role in Janussi’s murder, with a naming ceremony imminent that may replace her with Fembris Lancer or another candidate, and whose internal politics are being manipulated by Kalan’s academic strategy.
source_quote: The new head may give Bookwyrm one of two choices: continue as a member of the Avowed, or submit to a Zone of Truth.

subject: Ember Vanguard
fact: The Ember Vanguard is a rival faction that has become infamous underground, with exaggerated rumors and posters bearing the group's name, overshadowing the party's actual deeds.
source_quote: The Ember Vanguard, running ahead of us in every rumor, bigger and meaner than the four of us in a room arguing about a dead sage.

subject: Ember Vanguard
fact: The Ember Vanguard is a rival group whose legendary status overshadows the party, with exaggerated rumors and false posters in Gracklstugh bearing the party’s name — contributing to their infamy despite their desire to remain hidden.
source_quote: The Ember Vanguard has a legend now that walks a tunnel ahead of us, and it lies about our height.

subject: Ember Vanguard
fact: The Ember Vanguard is an infamous group that precedes the party in rumors, larger and more menacing, and has been falsely linked to their crimes in underground posters.
source_quote: The Ember Vanguard has a legend now that walks a tunnel ahead of us, and it lies about our height.

subject: The Avowed
fact: The Avowed are a scholarly order that opened the Alkrist safe and now oversee the detention of escapees; they have concluded their investigation prematurely, sealing the safe and assigning Kalan to guard duty, unaware of the theft.

subject: The Avowed
fact: The Avowed is a hierarchical organization undergoing leadership transition; internal power struggles are masked by public rituals of mourning and procedural formality, with members like Kalan and the Leader manipulating outcomes under the guise of justice.
source_quote: That will be done after the naming, by the new head of the Avowed.

subject: The Avowed
fact: The Avowed is the governing body of Candlekeep whose upcoming naming ceremony will determine the new head; its members are divided by suspicion, political maneuvering, and academic protocol, with Bookwyrm's fate in their hands.
source_quote: Bookwyrm is simply the current acting head of Candlekeep.

subject: The Avowed
fact: The Avowed is the governing body of the academic society that has been infiltrated by deception; its members are quick to accept Alkrist’s confession, seal evidence without scrutiny, and elevate Bookwyrm’s authority — revealing systemic complacency and institutional blindness.
source_quote: The Avowed had all decided they'd won.

subject: Unknown Architects of the Helmed Horrors
fact: An unseen faction designed and deployed helmed horrors as silent, untraceable assassins — creatures with no mouths, no minds, and no loyalty beyond a single objective: retrieve the inert key.
source_quote: Whoever built these chose them precisely so there'd be nobody to squeeze afterward.

subject: unknown creators of helmed horrors
fact: An unknown faction or force created the helmed horrors — sentient constructs designed for singular combat objectives, possibly linked to ancient arcane experiments or cursed armor smiths.
source_quote: Suits of plate with nobody inside, walking and hovering... They're like AIs.

subject: Alkrist's cell
fact: Alkrist is confined and finished — his confession, the cleaver, and the blood have sealed his fate.
source_quote: Alkrist is finished — his confession, the cleaver, the blood.

subject: Alkrist's prison cell
fact: Alkrist was held secure in the prisons, under guard, following his confession and implication of Bookwyrm.
source_quote: Alkrist will spend the day in the prisons, where he'll be kept secure and unable to escape.

subject: Alkrist's safe
fact: Alkrist's safe contained a potion of flying, a potion of superior healing, a fat purse of gold coins, and one red herring-stamped coin.
source_quote: A potion of flying. A potion of superior healing. A fat purse of gold coins, more than a man keeps for honest reasons. And one coin that did not match the rest. ... One of the gold coins had a herring stamped on it, and the herring was red.

subject: Alkrist's safe
fact: Alkrist's safe was opened in the presence of the Avowed and found to contain a potion of flying, healing potion, gold, and a red herring coin.
source_quote: A potion of flying. A potion of superior healing. A fat purse of gold coins... one of the gold coins had a herring stamped on it, and the herring was red.

subject: Ambush of the Helmed Horrors
fact: The ambush of the Helmed Horrors occurs in Deneir's Sanctum, where glass and wood enter from three directions, and helmed horrors hover a hand's width off the floor, their eyes glowing with points of light.
source_quote: Glass and wood came in at the same time, from three directions, and for a breath none of us had moved. ... Suits of plate with nobody inside, walking and — this was the part that made my neck itch — hovering, lifting a hand's width off the floor and drifting. Little points of light where eyes should be.

subject: Bookwyrm's chalice
fact: The heart was placed in the chalice of the statue by Bookwyrm — the central act of concealment.
source_quote: We think Bookwyrm extracted the heart and put it in the chalice of the statue, right?

subject: Bookwyrm's office
fact: Bookwyrm's office was arranged the way a room gets arranged when someone wants you to understand the seating before you sit, and the tea was already poured.
source_quote: Her office was arranged the way a room gets arranged when someone wants you to understand the seating before you sit. The tea was already poured.

subject: Bookwyrm's Office
fact: Bookwyrm’s office is arranged with deliberate intent — tea poured, chairs positioned — to assert control over the confrontation and force psychological compliance from the visitors.
source_quote: Her office was arranged the way a room gets arranged when someone wants you to understand the seating before you sit.

subject: Candlekeep
fact: Candlekeep is a revered library-fortress where scholarly authority and political power are intertwined; its internal politics are now the battleground for justice, with academic principles weaponized to avoid direct confrontation and preserve institutional stability.
source_quote: The reality is that all she did was hide a crime. She didn't commit one.

subject: Candlekeep
fact: Candlekeep is the destination where the party sought answers and unresolved questions from various scholars and keepers, including those related to Dawnbringer’s therapy and Janussi’s murder.
source_quote: the things we came to Candlekeep to ask the various folks, questions still owed to us.

subject: Candlekeep
fact: Candlekeep is the seat of the Avowed and the center of scholarly power where political and magical investigations into Bookwyrm's conduct are unfolding; its internal politics are shaped by precedent, suspicion, and academic ethics.
source_quote: Bookwyrm is simply the current acting head of Candlekeep.

subject: Candlekeep
fact: Candlekeep is the site of a naming ceremony for the new head of the Avowed, where suspicion, academic protocol, and power politics determine the fate of Bookwyrm.
source_quote: Tomorrow morning's naming ceremony clearly will not name her.

subject: Candlekeep library
fact: A magic book exists in the Candlekeep library that could prove Bookwyrm’s culpability — to be retrieved after the naming ceremony.
source_quote: There's got to be a book somewhere in the library we can use to actually get to the bottom of this.

subject: Candlekeep naming ceremony
fact: A naming ceremony for the new head of Candlekeep will occur tomorrow, and Bookwyrm is expected to be passed over.
source_quote: Tomorrow there will be a naming ceremony — and with all of this suspicion over her name, the confession, the information… the vote will go elsewhere.

subject: chalice of the statue
fact: The chalice of the statue contained the heart of Janussi, placed there by Bookwyrm to conceal the murder, and became the central physical clue in the investigation.
source_quote: She put the heart into the chalice of the statue.

subject: chalice of the statue
fact: The chalice of the statue was the container for the heart of Janussi, hidden as part of a cover-up orchestrated by Bookwyrm to protect Alkrist.
source_quote: She put the heart into the chalice of the statue.

subject: Chamber of Ambush
fact: The chamber was breached through its windows, littered with shattered glass, dust, and the remains of three destroyed helmed horrors, now reduced to rust and loose plate.
source_quote: Glass on the floor, dust settling, two dead heaps and one silent inert key...

subject: Deneir's Sanctum
fact: Deneir's Sanctum is a former office filled with books and scholarly artifacts, now used as a holding cell; it is under guard and has become the site of moral deliberation and quiet theft.

subject: Deneir's Sanctum
fact: Deneir's Sanctum is a locked room where the party was held captive before the ambush, now the site of a violent encounter with helmed horrors, filled with lingering tension and unresolved narrative weight.
source_quote: So we sat in Deneir's office, fed by proxy, our patient healed, wondering how the story was going to end.

subject: Deneir's Sanctum
fact: Deneir's Sanctum is a sealed chamber where the party was trapped during an ambush by helmed horrors, later left with shattered glass, dust, and two piles of ruined armor.
source_quote: Glass on the floor, dust settling, two dead heaps and one silent inert key three assassins had bled to reach.

subject: Deneir's Sanctum
fact: Deneir's Sanctum is the book-filled chamber repurposed as a holding cell, where the party is confined under guard — symbolizing their entrapment within Bookwyrm’s narrative despite their successes.
source_quote: They put us in Deneir's office to wait out the evening.

subject: Deneir's Sanctum
fact: Deneir's Sanctum is the designated destination for the adventurers after the confrontation; it serves as a place of temporary confinement under the pretense of protection.
source_quote: I will now ask Kalan Strongbranch to escort you to Deneir's Sanctum.

subject: Deneir's Sanctum
fact: Deneir's Sanctum is the location where Grygum waits before the ambush, where the party sits after the battle, and where the locked door prevents escape even after Daral is healed.
source_quote: Waiting in Deneir's Sanctum ... So we sat in Deneir's office, fed by proxy, our patient healed, wondering how the story was going to end.

subject: Deneir's Sanctum
fact: Deneir's Sanctum was filled with floor-to-ceiling bookshelves, tables, and the dry smell of old paper, and served as a guarded waiting room for the adventurers.
source_quote: They put us in Deneir's office to wait out the evening. Bookshelves floor to ceiling, tables, the dry smell of old paper — a room built for people who read for a living, now doing duty as a cell.

subject: Deneir's Sanctum
fact: The adventurers were escorted to Deneir's Sanctum to wait out the evening under guard.
source_quote: I will ask him to escort you to Deneir's Sanctum

subject: Deneir's Sanctum elevation
fact: Deneir's Sanctum is the room where the ambush occurred, with windows shattered and glass on the floor, the ceiling and walls breached by intruding armor.
source_quote: Glass and wood came in at the same time, from three directions... Glass on the floor, dust settling, two dead heaps and one silent inert key three assassins had bled to reach.

subject: Ember Vanguard's infamy
fact: The Ember Vanguard is infamous underground, with a legend that walks ahead of the party in every rumor, bigger and meaner than the four of them.
source_quote: The Ember Vanguard has a legend now that walks a tunnel ahead of us, and it lies about our height.

subject: Gracklstugh
fact: Gracklstugh is a location where the party is wanted on posters bearing their name, contributing to their underground infamy despite being misrepresented.
source_quote: Gracklstugh still had our name on posters, wrong enough to be cover but our name all the same.

subject: Gracklstugh
fact: Gracklstugh is referenced as a place where similar academic manipulations occurred, with the same pattern of using suspicion to destroy a target without direct accusation.
source_quote: I have seen this move before, in Gracklstugh, dressed in different robes.

subject: Gracklstugh posters
fact: Gracklstugh still has the party's name on posters — wrong enough to be cover but their name all the same.
source_quote: Gracklstugh still had our name on posters, wrong enough to be cover but our name all the same.

subject: Prisons of the Avowed
fact: The Prisons of the Avowed are where Alkrist is held under heavy guard; they serve as a tool of political control and a stage for public spectacle rather than genuine justice.
source_quote: Alkrist held secure in the prisons.

subject: Velkynvelve elevation
fact: Velkynvelve sits 100 feet above the cavern floor.
source_quote: Drow outpost was 100' in the sky

subject: chasme count
fact: Four chasme demons are present in the cavern above the prisoners' tower.
source_quote: four chasme and two vrock

subject: Dawnbringer
fact: Dawnbringer is a sentient sword that responded to Daral's praise by radiating warmth and grace, then later enhanced Thorin's strikes with sap-like slowing effects during combat, demonstrating sentience and emotional resonance.
source_quote: The blade lit, poured into Daral, and took the sickness with it." ... "the horror's movements went slow and sloppy, off-balance for its next swing.

subject: Glabbagool
fact: Glabbagool functions as a non-combative, absorptive entity — not an opponent, but a tool of quiet subterfuge — used to neutralize threats (like poisoned tea) without alerting observers.
source_quote: He held to it. No burp, no bubble, nothing.

subject: Glabbagool
fact: Glabbagool is a sentient ooze entity bonded to Grygum, capable of absorbing liquids, resisting acid, and executing silent theft — its behavior reflects training, restraint, and emerging autonomy.
source_quote: He took it. A faint singe of acid, a small heat under the skin of my arm as he burned it away — only I felt it.

subject: Glabbagool
fact: Glabbagool is an ooze-like entity fused to Zalthir's arm; it demonstrated autonomous predatory behavior by stealing the potion of flying and is now a latent threat with unknown capabilities.

subject: Glabbagool
fact: Glabbagool, the sentient arm of Zalthir, possesses autonomous agency and desires magical abilities; it actively sought and consumed the potion of flying, evaluating it as a 'good skill.'
source_quote: Under the skin of my arm, Glabbagool liked the flying skill. He thought it was a good skill.

subject: Helmed Horror
fact: Helmed Horrors are animated suits of plate armor with no occupants, capable of hovering a hand's width above the ground, emitting glowing points of light where eyes should be, and attacking with single-minded purpose to retrieve the inert key.
source_quote: Suits of plate with nobody inside, walking and — this was the part that made my neck itch — hovering, lifting a hand's width off the floor and drifting. Little points of light where eyes should be. ... They're like AIs," I said. Closest real-world frame I had. A thing built to do one thing, that would do it until you stopped it, and no amount of talking would move it off. ... The armored hand closed on nothing. Daz slipped it — barely, the kind of even you only call a win because the other guy didn't get you.

subject: Helmed Horror
fact: Helmed horrors are animated suits of plate armor with no occupants, capable of hovering and moving with eerie precision; they possess no sentience, speech, or emotion — only programmed objectives tied to the inert key.
source_quote: They're like AIs. A thing built to do one thing, that would do it until you stopped it, and no amount of talking would move it off.

subject: helmed horror
fact: Helmed horrors are animated suits of plate armor with no occupants, hovering slightly above ground, emitting glowing eye-points, and acting with single-minded, unyielding objectives — not responding to speech or emotion.
source_quote: Suits of plate with nobody inside, walking and — this was the part that made my neck itch — hovering, lifting a hand's width off the floor and drifting.

subject: helmed horror count
fact: Three helmed horrors are present in the ambush, suits of plate with nobody inside, hovering and drifting, with points of light where eyes should be.
source_quote: Glass and wood came in at the same time, from three directions, and for a breath none of us had moved. "Seems like it's a helmed horror?" ... Suits of plate with nobody inside, walking and — this was the part that made my neck itch — hovering, lifting a hand's width off the floor and drifting. Little points of light where eyes should be.

subject: Helmed Horrors
fact: Three helmed horrors, suits of animated plate armor with no mouths or minds, were sent to retrieve the key and were destroyed in combat after shifting targets based on the key’s movement.
source_quote: Three suits of murderous plate had come through the windows to die for it... A killer with no mouth and no mind.

subject: sword whisperer
fact: The party has been searching for a sword whisperer — a specialist who understands the psychological toll on blades — for Dawnbringer, who is built to carry such a weapon.
source_quote: I'd been the one hunting a sword whisperer for her since the road south — months where the thing she was built to carry just wasn't there

subject: the stench of suspicion
fact: The 'stench of suspicion' is not a creature but a metaphorical force actively shaping political outcomes; it is treated as a tangible threat that can destroy reputations without physical evidence.
source_quote: Even without evidence, the stench of suspicion will be all over her.

subject: the sword whisperer
fact: The sword whisperer is an elusive figure sought by Dawnbringer — a being who understands the psychological trauma of sentient weapons — and whose absence has left Dawnbringer emotionally unmoored, driving her need for therapy.
source_quote: I'd been the one hunting a sword whisperer for her since the road south — months where the thing she was built to carry just wasn't there.

subject: A'lai
fact: A'lai is a contender for the head of the Avowed but is not expected to be named, as suspicion and political momentum are directed elsewhere.
source_quote: A'lai won't be named either.

subject: A'lai
fact: A'lai is a figure of interest connected to the murder, with a thread running from the case back to him — but his role remains unclear, and the group has chosen not to confront him directly yet.
source_quote: We knew there was a thread running from all this back to A'lai.

subject: A'lai
fact: A'lai is a potential candidate for the new head of the Avowed, but is also suspected of being entangled in the case, and will not be named due to the surrounding suspicion.
source_quote: A'lai won't be named either.

subject: Alkrist
fact: Alkrist confessed to a crime (likely murder) involving poison, becoming the publicly accepted culprit — though others suspect Bookwyrm was the true architect and is covering for him as family.
source_quote: Kalan stepped in before the silence could set. 'But they have.' He began to lay it out — that Alkrist had stolen the — 'The poison.'

subject: Alkrist
fact: Alkrist confessed under Kalan's Zone of Truth spell to killing Janussi, and is believed to have murdered his nephew, with Bookwyrm covering for him.
source_quote: Alkrist had confessed. Kalan Strongbranch hadn't yet come back into the room, and we knew there was a thread running from all this back to A'lai.

subject: Alkrist
fact: Alkrist confessed under Kalan's Zone of Truth spell to killing Janussi, providing the conclusive piece of evidence in the murder mystery.
source_quote: Alkrist had said it out loud, in the room, with Kalan's spell still holding him honest — he'd killed Janussi.

subject: Alkrist
fact: Alkrist confessed under Kalan’s Zone of Truth spell to killing Janussi with a cleaver, but his confession does not explain who moved the heart or why — suggesting he is being used as a scapegoat to protect someone else.
source_quote: He'd killed Janussi.

subject: Alkrist
fact: Alkrist is deceased; his confession, the cleaver, and blood tie him to the central mystery, and his death has removed him as a political actor, leaving his legacy as a stain on Bookwyrm’s reputation.
source_quote: Alkrist is finished — his confession, the cleaver, the blood.

subject: Alkrist
fact: Alkrist is held securely in the prisons and accused of a grave crime, but evidence against him is circumstantial and potentially planted; he is the designated scapegoat in a larger political maneuver.
source_quote: Alkrist held secure in the prisons.

subject: Bookwyrm
fact: Bookwyrm hosted the group in her office with deliberate seating and poured tea as a psychological gesture, calmly drinking it while accusing them of relying on weak proof — implying her innocence and control over the narrative.
source_quote: She drank some, watching us over the rim. 'With all this talk of murder in the house, I think a little tea is good for soothing the nerves.'

subject: Bookwyrm
fact: Bookwyrm is referenced by herself as the one who drank tea while watching the adventurers over the rim, and who claimed that tea was good for soothing the nerves after talk of murder.
source_quote: And she drank some, watching us over the rim. ... With all this talk of murder in the house, I think a little tea is good for soothing the nerves.

subject: Bookwyrm
fact: Bookwyrm is suspected of hiding a crime by placing a heart in the chalice of a statue to protect Alkrist, and faces potential removal from her position at Candlekeep due to suspicion and academic protocol.
source_quote: She didn't commit one — but she hid a crime.

subject: Bookwyrm
fact: Bookwyrm is the current acting head of Candlekeep and the central figure of suspicion due to her association with a confession, a cleaver, and blood; her election as permanent head is under threat, and her fate hinges on whether she submits to a Zone of Truth or declines it.
source_quote: Bookwyrm is simply the current acting head of Candlekeep.

subject: Bookwyrm
fact: Bookwyrm is the current acting head of Candlekeep, suspected of concealing evidence in Janussi’s murder by moving the victim’s heart into the statue’s chalice, and is under threat of removal due to mounting suspicion — though her innocence has not been proven.
source_quote: She walks.

subject: Bookwyrm
fact: Bookwyrm is the leader of the Avowed who declared the safe of no further interest; she is weary of the spectacle and has ordered the group to be escorted to their chambers, unaware that the potion of flying has been removed.

subject: Bookwyrm
fact: Bookwyrm is the manipulative Avowed leader who feigns grief and outrage while secretly relieved that Alkrist’s confession shields her — she orchestrates the group’s isolation, allows the safe to be sealed with incriminating evidence, and ensures her own elevation by appearing cooperative.
source_quote: Alkrist. I could never have imagined it.

subject: Daral
fact: Daral feared being left broken because the party had decided he wasn't worth the spell.
source_quote: under the scholarship, the small fear of being left broken because we'd decided he wasn't worth the spell

subject: Daral
fact: Daral is an escapee who has shifted from arrogance to quiet desperation, now openly pleading for his own cure while internally fearing he is not worth the spell.

subject: Daral
fact: Daral, recently restored by Dawnbringer, panicked during the ambush, claiming helmed horrors cannot be here, revealing his fragile mental state despite physical recovery.
source_quote: Behind us Daral was coming apart, saying it wasn't possible, these creatures can't be here, how could they.

subject: Dawnbringer
fact: Dawnbringer is a sentient entity who communicates telepathically, seeks therapeutic intervention for blade-related trauma, and is identified by the party as female despite uncertainty about her nature.
source_quote: She could make noises in my head... I thought Dawnbringer was a she... Whatever — she. Yeah, I think we said she.

subject: Dawnbringer
fact: Dawnbringer is a telepathic entity who has been hunting a sword whisperer since the road south, and now seeks further therapeutic sessions to understand the psychological toll of the search.
source_quote: I'd been the one hunting a sword whisperer for her since the road south — months where the thing she was built to carry just wasn't there.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz believes patience is a viable strategy if it leads to action.
source_quote: Wait and see if people figure it out.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz is a spellcaster who initially misjudged the nature of the helmed horrors but quickly adapted, realizing they were drawn to a key in his pocket — a key invisible to all detection magic.
source_quote: They don't have feelings. They have objectives.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz is an escapee who communicates in cryptic numerical shorthand; he suggested Fembris as taster using '118' and remains undecided on whether to cure Daral, embodying cautious deliberation.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz is perceptive and attuned to hidden motives; he recognized the Leader’s dual intent — genuine concern and calculated containment — and interpreted the situation as a strategic trap.
source_quote: Daz found the other half, the half I only saw land on his face: she was delighted to have us wrapped up and out of everything, no more heads poking anywhere.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz is referenced by himself as the one who offered '118' as a taster protocol for the food, meaning nothing to Fembris and everything to the group.
source_quote: I'd say 118,

subject: Daz
fact: Daz is the observational tactician who applies narrative theory to interrogation — he detects the seam in Bookwyrm’s performance and advocates for withholding information to provoke deception, but remains passive in action.
source_quote: My take: be a little shy with the full details, but give enough to make it look like they could tell a story.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz is the one who holds the inert key that triggers the helmed horrors' attack, survives being targeted by them, and after the battle, is assured by Grygum he will be fine.
source_quote: Behind us Daral was coming apart, saying it wasn't possible, these creatures can't be here, how could they. ... Daz passed the key to Grygum and threw the last of what he had at the one he'd been burning — three darts of light, all home. ... 'Ouch,' Daz said. 'I may drink a healing.' ... 'Don't you worry, Daz. You're going to be fine. Totally fine.'

subject: Daz
fact: Daz is the one who was targeted by helmed horrors, later discovers the key in his pocket is the true object of their attack, and casts Scorching Ray to damage them.
source_quote: Behind us Daral was coming apart, saying it wasn't possible, these creatures can't be here, how could they. Fembris just stood in shock. I clocked both of them and put them out of my head. Panicking men are terrain you can't use. ... Daz went hunting through his spells and landed on the wrong idea first — something about breaking their minds — before the truth caught up. ... Daz passed the key to Grygum and threw the last of what he had at the one he'd been burning — three darts of light, all home.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz is the pragmatic contingency planner, always ready with a fallback plan of violence — 'hacking and slashing' — as a safety net when diplomacy or academia fails.
source_quote: If things go sideways, we can always start hacking and slashing.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz provided the fallback contingency of 'hacking and slashing' whenever the group’s plans became too abstract or risky.
source_quote: If things go sideways, we can always start hacking and slashing.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz provides a pragmatic fallback plan of violent escalation — hacking and slashing — as a contingency when diplomatic or strategic options fail.
source_quote: If things go sideways, we can always start hacking and slashing.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz relies on the option of hacking and slashing as a comforting contingency plan.
source_quote: If things go sideways, we can always start hacking and slashing.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz was nearly knocked unconscious by a single blow and carried a key that emitted no magical signature, which attracted the attention of the helmed horrors.
source_quote: I may drink a healing. Which is Daz's way of telling you he was one bad swing from the floor.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz was still weighing whether to cure Daral.
source_quote: I mean, if he's… I don't know," Daz said, which is Daz for *I'm still weighing it, and it hasn't landed yet.*

subject: Daz
fact: Daz was targeted by helmed horrors during the ambush, survived a crushing blow, and cast Scorching Ray to damage them, demonstrating adaptability after realizing they lack minds.
source_quote: Alright — we're going to try Scorching Ray.

subject: Fembris
fact: Fembris is a passive observer who witnessed the key being passed and may hold critical but unacknowledged information about the ambush’s origin.
source_quote: When Grygum handed the key to Daz — who saw it? Fembris. Standing right there with the four of us.

subject: Fembris
fact: Fembris stood in shock during the helmed horrors' ambush, unresponsive and mentally overwhelmed, treated as terrain by Thorin due to inaction.
source_quote: Fembris just stood in shock.

subject: Fembris
fact: Fembris was present when the key was first observed and is the only known witness to its prior state before the ambush.
source_quote: When Grygum handed the key to Daz — who saw it? Fembris. Standing right there with the four of us.

subject: Fembris Lancer
fact: Fembris Lancer is a likely candidate to replace Bookwyrm as head of the Avowed, suggested by Kalan as the next leader who would be more willing to pursue justice against Bookwyrm after the naming ceremony.
source_quote: Fembris Lancer will probably get elected the new avowed...

subject: Fembris Lancer
fact: Fembris Lancer is imprisoned in Deneir's Sanctum and serves as an unwilling companion to the escapees; he is trusted by no one but eats without suspicion, making him the group's designated food taster.

subject: Fembris Lancer
fact: Fembris Lancer is referenced by Grygum as the one who sat silently during arguments and later served as the group's food taster, eating without suspicion.
source_quote: Fembris Lancer had stood off to one side the whole time we argued, saying nothing, which I respected. ... Fembris, on the other hand, had no such reservations — come, come, come, already reaching, all appetite and no suspicion.

subject: Fembris Lancer
fact: Fembris Lancer is the anticipated successor to Bookwyrm as head of the Avowed, elected by default due to the collapse of Bookwyrm’s credibility.
source_quote: Fembris Lancer will probably get elected the new avowed.

subject: Fembris Lancer
fact: Fembris Lancer is the likely candidate to be elected the new head of the Avowed, as suspicion surrounding Bookwyrm and Alkrist has shifted political favor toward her.
source_quote: Fembris Lancer will probably get elected the new avowed.

subject: Fembris Lancer
fact: Fembris Lancer is the passive observer and unwitting taster who, despite being under suspicion, remains naive and trusting — his consumption of the food serves as a risk-spending tool for the party’s survival calculus.
source_quote: Fembris, on the other hand, had no such reservations — come, come, come, already reaching, all appetite and no suspicion.

subject: Glabbagool
fact: Glabbagool is Grygum’s sentient, acid-resistant ooze companion who absorbs liquids and magic, silently steals the potion of flying, and demonstrates nascent discipline by acting only on whispered instruction.
source_quote: Under the skin of my arm, Glabbagool liked the flying skill. He thought it was a good skill.

subject: Glabbagool

subject: Zone of Truth

subject: Zone of Truth spell
fact: The Zone of Truth spell does not guarantee truth-telling but reveals whether a subject can resist its effect; it is a tool of pressure, not compulsion, and can be countered by mental fortitude, making its use politically delicate.

subject: Zone of Truth spell
fact: The Zone of Truth spell is a magical effect that compels honesty, but it is not infallible — it can be resisted with mental discipline, and its true value lies not in extracting truth, but in revealing whether someone *can* lie.
source_quote: The spell doesn't hand you the truth. It hands you the ability to watch someone refuse it.

subject: Zone of Truth spell

subject: moral compromise of scholarly protocol
